content.title: How to watch UConn vs. Illinois in Final Four: Time, TV
content.text: UConn's Alex Karaban (11) laughs alongside teammate Braylon Mullins (24) and Jaylin Stewart (3) during practice ahead of a national semifinal NCAA college basketball tournament game against Illinois at the Final Four, Friday, April 3, 2026, in Indianapolis. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)Abbie Parr/Associated PressINDIANAPOLIS — When Keaton Wagler played against the UConn men's basketball team back on Nov. 28 at Madison Square Garden, he was merely a freshman.When he faces the Huskies again on Saturday in the Final Four, Wagler will be more than just a freshman. He's a second-team All-American, Most Outstanding Player from the South Regional and one of the top freshmen in a season full of great ones.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢"It's crazy where he's come," said Braylon Mullins, a not-too-shabby freshman himself. "He's an incredible player. Just seeing his role completely shift throughout the year, he's doing his thing."That "thing" includes averaging 17.9 points per game. Wagler, an unheralded recruit, was averaging just 13.5 per game after scoring a season-low three points on 1-for-3 shooting in a season-low 14 minutes in that Black Friday loss to UConn.Since then, Wagler has scored in double figures in all 27 of the Illini's games. He was never better than on Jan. 24 at Purdue, when he set a Big Ten freshman record with 46 points on 13-for-17 shooting (9-for-11 from 3) in an Illinois victory.Illinois guard Keaton Wagler, center, fights for a loose ball with UConn guard Malachi Smith, right, and Solo Ball, left, during the second half of an NCAA college basketball game Friday, Nov. 28, 2025, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)Adam Hunger/Associated Press"That kind of changed his trajectory," Silas Demary Jr. said of Wagler's poor outing against UConn. "He started taking off and was killing it in every game. He kind of took over the team as a leader."Article continues below this adMake CT Insider a preferred source on Google to see more of our journalism when you search.Add Preferred SourceDan Hurley, as he'll do, had a slightly contrarian view."We did a decent job guarding him," the coach noted. "He was playing well going into our game. It's not like he wasn't playing well. He was one of their most talented players then.""He was still on the scouting report as a good player, a scorer," added junior Jaylin Stewart. "We tried to take him out of the game, and we did."Article continues below this adWhat did the Huskies do so effectively against Wagler, a 6-foot-6 guard? Solo Ball, not known for his defensive prowess, began the game guarding him."I think it was more of a team approach," Ball recalled. "But you have to be physical, make it as tough on him as possible. Even with (Kylan) Boswell, they've got two great guards. To be able to contain both of them is going to be important."Boswell, in fact, led the Illini with 25 points in the loss to UConn. The 6-2 point guard's mid-season injury that kept him out of seven games opened the door for Wagler to take over as the team's point guard and de facto leader.INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - APRIL 03: Head coach Dan Hurley of the UConn Huskies looks on during the Practice Day of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Lucas Oil Stadium on April 03, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty ImagesOf course, Illinois is hardly a one-man show. It's "Balkan 5" of David Mirkovic, Tomislav Ivisic, Andrej Sojakovic, Zvonimir Ivisic and Mihailo Petrovic helped engineer one of the most prolific, efficient offenses in the nation. Article continues below this adBut Wagler has emerged as the straw that stirs the drink."I know that game he didn't have a big impact," Mullins said. "But there were some guys on our team that didn't have a big impact. It's going to be a new game."Hurley noted that UConn is implementing some "fundamental, tactical, strategic things" that can get Ball, Mullins and Alex Karaban (all of whom have struggled shooting on anything but 35-footers lately) better looks."Especially Solo and Braylon," Hurley said. "So, we're excited to try to implement that with those guys."Article continues below this adNo. 2 UConn vs. No. 3 IllinoisWhat: NCAA Tournament Final FourWhere: Lucas Oil Stadium, IndianapolisWhen: Saturday, 6:09 p.m.Article continues below this adRecords: UConn 33-5, Illinois 28-8TV: TBSRadio: UConn Sports Network, Fox Sports Radio 97.9, WAVZ-New Haven (1300 AM), WGCH- Greenwich (1490 AM), WICH-Norwich (1310 AM, 94.5 FM), WILI-Willimantic (1400 AM, 95.3 FM)ILLINOISArticle continues below this adPlayer Pos. PPG Article continues below this adSolo Ball G 12.9Silas Demary Jr. G 10.4Tarris Reed Jr. C 14.7Article continues below this adAlex Karaban F 13.2Braylon Mullins F 11.9Get daily updates from the UConn basketball world.April 3, 2026Dave Borges is a sports reporter for Hearst Connecticut Media Group covering the UConn men's basketball team. An award-winning journalist, Dave has covered the Huskies since 2007, including coverage of five Final Fours and four national championships (2011, 2014, 2023 and 2024). He has been an Associated Press Top 25 poll voter since 2009 and was named NSMA Connecticut Sportswriter of the Year in 2019. Dave has authored three books: "Hurley's Heroes: UConn's Return to College Basketball's Elite," "Rebound: The Incredible Story of UConn Basketball's Comeback from Defeat to Dominance," and "Images of Baseball: The Pawtucket Red Sox." He also covers baseball and was a beat writer chronicling the 2004 World Series-champion Boston Red Sox. Dave has been a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 2014.
